meetings.summary: In this meeting the committee discussed issuing a press statement announcing its advice to the President to reinstate Mr. Mahmoud Riyaz, the former Deputy Commissioner of the Maldives Customs Service. This recommendation followed the committee’s review of the incidents involving the smuggling of cigarette cartons on a vessel belonging to The Hawks Private Limited and the illegal release of cigarettes from a bonded warehouse without the authority of the Maldives Customs Service. meetings.title: 4th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the committee conducted interviews on the issue of the selection of two members from the public to the Police Board by parliament in accordance with Section 75(d) of the Maldives Police Service Act, 2020. In this regard, the following individuals were interviewed: · Ahmed Muawiyath Qasim · Ahmed Mizmadh · Mohamed Sadiq · Nisbah Hassan (Referral: Ahmed Mubeen) After interviewing all the candidates, marks were awarded as per the criteria set by the Committee on General Purposes in awarding marks to the interviewees as per Section 223(c) of the Standing Order of Peoples’ Majlis. At the end of the interview, of all the candidates who appeared for the interview, MP Ahmed Saleem of Eydhafushi Constituency, the chair of the committee, proposed those who have scored an average of 75% (seventy-five percent) or above are eligible to be selected to the Police Board from the general public under Section 75(d) of the Maldives Police Service Act, 2020, therefore to send their names to the floor. The voting details for this proposal are on “Vote 1” of “Votes” section of this page. This proposal was unanimously passed by the members attended and voted.

meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: The agenda for today’s meeting is to review the issue of the selection of two members from the public to the Police Board by parliament in accordance with Section 75(d) of the Maldives Police Service Act, 2020. When the floor was opened for members, MP Mohamed Nazim of North Maafannu Constituency proposed, and MP Abdulla Shareef of Kelaa Constituency seconded to set the deadline of the issue to 13 th March 2025. The voting details for this proposal are on “Vote 1” of “Votes” section of this page. This proposal was unanimously passed by the members attended and voted. After that, when the floor was opened for members, MP Abdulla Shareef of Kelaa Constituency proposed and MP Mohamed Shahid of Hulhudhoo Constituency seconded to follow the procedure for interviewing and awarding marks in accordance with the "Criteria to be Followed for Awarding Marks to the Interviewees for Appointment to Independent Institutions and Autonomous Posts" approved by the Committee on General Purposes of Parliament under Section 223(c) of the Standing Order of Parliament. The voting details for this proposal are on “Vote 2” of “Votes” section of this page. This proposal was unanimously passed by the members attended and voted. Also MP Abdulla Shareef of Kelaa Constituency proposed and MP Mohamed Shahid of Hulhudhoo Constituency seconded to conduct the interviews on 12 March 2025. The voting details for this proposal are on “Vote 3” of “Votes” section of this page. This proposal was unanimously passed by the members attended and voted. After that, the chair of the committee, MP Ahmed Saleem of Eydhafushi Constituency porposed Assistant Director General, Legal Affairs Dr. Aminath Asfa Shafie, Deputy Director, Legal Affairs Uza. Shiraza Naseer and Legal Officer Mr. Mohamed Harees Haneef as the administrative panel in accordance with Section 223 of the Standing Order to conduct the interview process. Since none of the members objected to the proposal, it was decided to proceed with it. After that, members discussed the issue of security forces carrying out a special operation related to national security on the night of 10 March 2025. After discussions among the members, it was decided to write to the Maldives Police Service and the Ministry of Defence requesting information related to the operation to the committee. After that, the committee discussed the ongoing investigation into the smuggling of cigarette cartons on an oil tanker owned by The Hawks Private Limited, which is being reviewed by the committee. MP Abdul Gafoor Moosa of Hanimaadhoo Constituency proposed and MP Mohamed Shahid of Hulhudhoo Constituency seconded the committee members to visit the storage location of where the confiscated cigarette cartons stored by Maldives Customs Service. The voting details for this proposal are on “Vote 4” of “Votes” section of this page. This proposal was unanimously passed by the members attended and voted.

meetings.title: 13th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: The agenda for today’s meeting was continuation of evaluating the Bill on Amendment to Employment Act (Act No: 2/2008). Each provision in the bill was read separately. North Maafannu Constituency Member Mohamed Nazim proposed, and Maamigili Constituency Member Qaasim Ibrahim seconded to add the following statement at the end of section 65-5 (e) (4).“The deposit amount shall not exceed the cost of repatriation of the employee.” This proposal was passed by majority vote. Hithadhoo Central Constituency Member Ahmed Azaan Marzooq proposed, and Hulhudhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Shaahidh seconded to keep the the clause 65-5 (i) as it is. This proposal was passed by majority vote. After that, two proposals came on section 65-7 (a) (2). First Proposal: Central Hithadhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Azaan Marzooq proposed, and Hulhudhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Shaahidh seconded to keep the clause of MVR 50,000 Mvr fine as it is. Second Proposal: Maafannu Uthuru Constituency Member Mohamed Naazim and Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim seconded the proposal to set a range of MVR 5,000 to MVR 50,000 Mvr range for the fine instead of MVR 50,000 Mvr because it is too severe. After discussions, the vote for the first proposal was passed with the majority vote including the committee chair. It was then asked for a vote to pass the bill from the committee along with changes proposed and passed by the committee. The bill was passed by majority vote.

meetings.title: 12th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: At today’s meeting, the committee started evaluating the Bill on Amendment to Employment Act (Act No: 2/2008) by reading each provision of the amendment bill. Hanimaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed to change the phrasing of 65(a). After discussing among the members off the record it was eventually decided to keep the wordings of the phrase as it is, and no other member objected to it. After that, members discussed changing the phrasing of 65 (c) from “shall not take part in employment” to “taking part in employment is prohibited”. It was proposed by, Hanimaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Gafoor Moosa and seconded by Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim. This proposal was passed unanimously. Members then discussed about changing the phrasing of 65-1 (a) from “ministry may decide” to “ministry shall decide”. It was proposed by, Hanimaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Gafoor Moosa and seconded by Thulhaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Hannaan Aboobakuru. This proposal was passed unanimously. Following that, members discussed changing the phrasing of 65-1 (b) from “may decide” to “shall decide” and add “make it public twice a year of the number of quotas allocated to each sector and the number of quotas allotted” to this clause. . It was proposed by, Hanimaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Gafoor Moosa and seconded by Maafannu Uthuru Constituency Member Mohamed Naazim. This proposal was passed unanimously. Moreover, members discussed about the comments received from Maldives Trade Union and Maldives Health Professionals Union on section 65-1 (e) (4) of the bill. Hanimaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Gafoor Moosa Proposed and Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim seconded to disregard the comments on this clause and keep the clause as it is. This proposal was passed unanimously. After that, members discussed about the comments received from Maldives Trade Union and Maldives Health Professionals Union on section 65-1 (e) (5) of the bill. Maafannu Uthuru Constituency Member Mohamed Naazim proposed and Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim seconded to disregard the comments on this clause and keep the clause as it is. This proposal was passed unanimously. Additionally, members also discussed about section 65-1 (g) & (h) of the bill and Maafannu Uthuru Constituency Member Mohamed Naazim proposed and Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim seconded to keep the clause as it is. This proposal was passed unanimously. After that, members discussed about the 2,000 (two thousand) rufiyaa fee mentioned in clause 65-4 (c) and Hanimaadho Constituency Member Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed to remove this fee but no other member seconded this proposal. Therefore, it was decided to keep this clause as it is. Furthermore, members discussed about, 65-4 (e) (2) which is about revising and increasing the fee. Two proposals were received for this proposal. They are: 1. Maafannu Uthuru Constituency Member Mohamed Naazim proposed and Hanimaadho Constituency Member Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed to reduce the percentage from 30% to 10%. 2. Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim proposed to remove the clauses of 65-4 (d) & (e) despite no other member seconded this proposal. The committee then decided to take a decision on these clauses in the next meeting after further deliberation on the fees in the bill and further consideration by the members.

meetings.title: 11th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: The agenda for today’s meeting was to set a deadline for the Bill on Amendment to Employment Act (Act No: 2/2008) and decide how to proceed with getting feedback and comments for the bill from the public and other institutions. When the floor was opened to members, Maafannu Uthuru Constituency Member Mohamed Naazim proposed, and Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim supported the deadline of the bill to set for 13 th of August 2024. Below are the voting details for this proposal. Vote: Set 13 th August 2024 as deadline of the bill. Total number of members: 13 Number of members present: 8 Voted Yes: 7 (Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim, Maafannu Uthuru Constituency Member Mohamed Naazim, Kelaa Constituency Member Abdulla Shareef, Hanimaadho Constituency Member Abdul Gaffor Moosa, Thulhaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Hannaan Aboobakuru, Hithadhoo Central Constituency Member Ahmed Azaan Marzooq, Dhiggaru Constituency Member Ahmed Naazim) Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Total voted: 11 Required to Pass: 6 Result: Passed Hence, the proposal to set 13 August 2024 as deadline of the bill was passed by the consensus of the present members voted. At this point, Inguraidoo Constituency Member Ibrahim Falah, Mahibadhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Tariq and Kashidhoo Constituency Member Muntazim Ibrahim have joined the committee. Next Dhiggaru Constituency Member Ahmed Naazim proposed and Thulhaadhoo constituency Abdul Hannaan Aboobakuru supported to open the bill for public comments and send for other institutions for their feedback. Below are the voting details for this proposal. Vote: Open the bill for public comments and share with state other institutions for their feedback. Total number of members: 13 Number of members present: 11 Voted Yes: 10 (Maamigili Constituency Member Qasim Ibrahim, Maafannu Uthuru Constituency Member Mohamed Naazim, Kelaa Constituency Member Abdulla Shareef, Hanimaadho Constituency Member Abdul Gaffor Moosa, Thulhaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Hannaan Aboobakuru, Hithadhoo Central Constituency Member Ahmed Azaan Marzooq, Dhiggaru Constituency Member Ahmed Naazim, Inguraidhoo Constituency Member Ibrahim Falaah, Mahibadhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Thoariq, Kaashidhoo Constituency Member Munthasim Ibrahim) Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Total voted: 10 Required to Pass: 6 Result: Passed Hence, the proposal to open the bill for public comments and share with state other institutions for their feedback was passed by the consensus of present members. At this point, Hulhudhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Shaahidh Joined the Meeting.
